newsitem.title: ITALY: Rome dumps newly-appointed ambassador to Tirana.
newsitem.headline: Rome dumps newly-appointed ambassador to Tirana.

text.p: Italy said on Sunday it had revoked the appointment of its new ambassador to Albania because he had shown in published remarks that he was not the right candidate for the job.

The decision came only days after Manfredo Incisa di Camerana had been appointed and a week after Paolo Foresti, the ambassador he was to have replaced, also plunged into controversy over allegations of bias.

The Foreign Ministry said in a short statement that "it notes that following the offer by ambassador Manfredo Incisa di Camerana to renounce the appointment bestowed on him, the government has decided to revoke the nomination."

Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini later told the Ansa news agency that the decision was due to "somewhat disconcerting" comments by Incisa published on Saturday. He denied the change would damage Italy's image abroad.

Incisa, a former ambassador to Mozambique, was quoted in the La Repubblica newspaper on Saturday as saying that the Italian Foreign Ministry was going through a period of weakness and Foresti had always been politically-aligned.
The newspaper quoted him on Sunday as saying that his comments had been off the record and were distorted. At the same time, he had offered to stand down from the post.
Dini said the decision to accept his offer and revoke the nomination was "a particular event involving an individual who has not shown himself to be up to the situation."
"The situation in Albania is delicate but there is no immediate urgency. We have an ambassador with a lot of experience who has finished his mandate: He should have been recalled some time ago.
"In the next few days we will have a new nomination."
The announcement came as Prime Minister Romano Prodi was due to visit Albania and was a further headache for Italy over its embassy in the Balkan country.
Prodi was due to reach Tirana on Sunday afternoon and meet Berisha and Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.

Foresti, who was due to be replaced last December after completing his tour of duty but stayed on after crisis in the country, was accused by an Albanian opposition newspaper of bias in favour of embattled president Sali Berisha.
The newspaper Indipendent carried a purported transcript of a telephone conversation between Foresti and the chairman of Berisha's Democratic Party, Tritan Shehu.

In the published exchange, which Foresti said was fabricated, the envoy appeared to try to undermine the role of European mediator Franz Vranitzky and to offer to help broker a deal with the Albanian opposition in Berisha's favour.
Dini stated publicly at the time that the purported remarks "do not correspond to the Italian government's position".

Italy, with strong trade ties to Albania and eager to stem an influx of illegal immigrants from across the Adriatic, has played an active part in international attempts to brake the impoverished state's slide into anarchy.

It leads a multinational military force deployed in Albania following rioting and looting in February and March after anger at the collapse of shady investment schemes mushroomed into an uprising against Berisha in the south of the country.

Dini has championed the installation in March of a nine-party national unity government led by opposition Socialist Bashkim Fino under an accord designed to lead to early parliamentary elections on June 29.
